NHIA KNOWLEDGE BASE

SOURCE 6 — Policy Documents & Legal Framework

Acts · Regulations · Guidelines · NHIA governance

SOURCE

NHIS Policy Documents & Legal Framework (2025)

CATEGORY

policy, legal-framework

INTENT

Explain the legal basis, structure, and governance of the NHIS to members and agents

Section 1 — Overview & Timeline

CHUNK 1 — NHIS Legal Framework Overview

The NHIS of Ghana is governed by a comprehensive legal framework establishing rights, responsibilities, and operational procedures for universal health coverage.

Key milestones:

2003 — National Health Insurance Act, 2003 (Act 650) enacted — original framework

2004 — NHIS operations commenced

2008 — National Health Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2008 (Act 753)

2012 — National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852) — CURRENT governing legislation

2012 onwards — Various Legislative Instruments and Guidelines issued

Act 852 repealed both Acts 650 and 753. It was assented to on October 31, 2012.

It is organised into 4 parts covering 113 sections.

[category: policy]  [tags: legal framework, Act 852, timeline, history, legislation]

CHUNK 2 — Hierarchy of Legal Documents

Level 1 — Acts of Parliament (highest authority) — e.g. Act 852

Level 2 — Legislative Instruments (L.I.) — made by Minister/NHIA

Level 3 — Regulations and Guidelines — issued by NHIA Board

Level 4 — Operational Manuals and Procedures — issued by NHIA

Any conflict between levels is resolved in favour of the higher-level document.

Section 111 of Act 852 provides consequential amendments to related Acts to ensure consistency.

[category: policy]  [tags: hierarchy, legislation, L.I., regulations, guidelines, authority]

Section 2 — Act 852: Structure and Key Provisions

2.1 Structure of Act 852

CHUNK 3 — Act 852 Structure (4 Parts, 113 Sections)

Part One (Sections 1–25): National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)

— Establishment, object, functions, Board composition, committees, accounts, auditing

Part Two (Sections 26–52): National Health Insurance Scheme

— Membership, registration, contributions, exemptions, benefits package,

— Credentialing of healthcare providers, medicines & services lists,

— Claims, provider payment, NHIF, National Health Insurance Levy

Part Three (Sections 53–105): Private Health Insurance Schemes

— Types of private schemes, registration, licensing, operational requirements, supervision

Part Four (Sections 106–113): Adjudication and Other Provisions

— Adjudication Committee, offences and penalties, regulations, transitional provisions

[category: policy]  [tags: Act 852, structure, parts, sections, NHIA, scheme]

2.2 Key Provisions

CHUNK 4 — Mandatory Membership (Section 27)

All residents of Ghana are required to belong to the National Health Insurance Scheme.

Employers must ensure that their employees are registered.

Source: Section 27, National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852)

[category: policy]  [tags: mandatory membership, registration, employers, Section 27]

CHUNK 5 — Exemptions from Contributions (Section 29)

The following categories are exempt from paying NHIS premiums:

— Children below 18 years

— Pregnant women

— Persons with mental disorders

— Indigents

— Differently-abled persons (as determined by the Minister)

— SSNIT pensioners and contributors

— Persons above 70 years of age

Approximately 65% of active NHIS members fall under exempted categories.

Exempted members may still be required to pay a small processing fee for registration/renewal.

Source: Section 29, National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852)

[category: policy]  [tags: exemptions, premium, contributions, children, pregnant, SSNIT, elderly, indigent, Section 29]

CHUNK 6 — National Health Insurance Fund (Sections 39–46)

Sources of funding for the NHIS:

— 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy on goods and services

— 2.5% of SSNIT contributions

— Parliamentary allocations

— Investment returns

— Member premiums

— Grants and donations

The levy is collected by the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) under Act 791.

Source: Sections 39–46, Act 852

[category: policy]  [tags: NHIF, funding, levy, SSNIT, 2.5%, contributions, fund]

Section 3 — Legislative Instruments & Regulations

CHUNK 7 — Legislative Instrument 1809 (L.I. 1809)

L.I. 1809 established the original NHIS benefit package and operational framework.

Note: Some provisions of L.I. 1809 were superseded by Act 852 (2012).

Section 108 of Act 852 empowers the Minister to make regulations on:

— Registration of members and health insurance identity cards

— Contributions and mode of payment

— Healthcare benefits under the scheme

— Means test for exemptions

— Credentialing of healthcare providers

— Suspension of membership

— Quality assurance of services

— Determination and payment of tariffs

— Claims submission and processing

— Dispute resolution procedures

— Exemptions from the National Health Insurance Levy

[category: policy]  [tags: L.I. 1809, regulations, Section 108, minister, tariffs, claims, credentialing]

Section 4 — Guidelines and Operational Documents

CHUNK 8 — NHIS Medicines List

Updated annually. Latest edition: March 2025.

Contains 551 approved medicines derived from the Essential Medicines List.

Lists medicines by generic (International Non-Proprietary) names — NOT brand names.

Includes dosage forms and pricing for each entry.

Only credentialed providers can prescribe NHIS medicines.

Patients should ensure their prescription uses the exact generic name from this list.

Personal abbreviations or brand-only names are not accepted on NHIS claims forms.

[category: policy]  [tags: medicines list, 551, formulary, generic, 2025]

CHUNK 9 — NHIS Tariff Operation Manual (2022)

Latest version: 2022.

Covers service lists and tariffs for all covered services.

Includes the Ghana Diagnostic Related Groupings (G-DRG) system.

Outpatient department tariffs by specialty.

Provider payment methodologies.

The G-DRG system groups approximately 500 specific diagnosis and procedure codes.

Tariffs define how much NHIA pays a provider for each service.

[category: policy]  [tags: tariff, G-DRG, services, payment, 2022, OPD]

CHUNK 10 — Credentialing Guidelines

Standards for healthcare provider accreditation by NHIA.

Quality assessment tools as per Act 852 and L.I. 1809.

Grading system for facilities.

Re-accreditation procedures.

NHIA works in collaboration with HEFRA (Health Facilities Regulatory Agency) for credentialing.

Only credentialed (accredited) facilities can provide NHIS-covered services.

Credentialing complaints: credentialing@nhia.gov.gh

[category: policy]  [tags: credentialing, accreditation, HEFRA, grading, provider, quality]

CHUNK 11 — Claims Processing Guidelines

Submission formats and procedures for providers.

Processing timelines defined by NHIA.

Validation and verification procedures.

Payment schedules.

Note for members: if a facility says NHIA has not paid them and therefore you must pay out-of-pocket,

this is NOT a valid reason to charge a covered NHIS member.

Report such incidents to 0544446447 or info@nhia.gov.gh.

[category: policy]  [tags: claims, submission, processing, payment, provider]

Section 5 — Related Legal Framework

5.1 Acts Referenced in Act 852

Act

Relevance

Insurance Act, 2006 (Act 724)

Applies to private commercial health insurance schemes

Companies Act, 1963 (Act 179)

Registration requirements for private health insurance schemes

Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843)

Member data privacy and security requirements

Internal Audit Agency Act, 2003 (Act 658)

Internal audit requirements for NHIA

Ghana Revenue Authority Act, 2009 (Act 791)

Collection of National Health Insurance Levy

Hospitals Fees Act, 1971 (Act 387)

Act 852 prevails in case of conflict

CHUNK 12 — Regulatory Agencies

HEFRA (Health Facilities Regulatory Agency):

Mandated to register, license, and monitor all healthcare facilities in Ghana.

Works in collaboration with NHIA for credentialing purposes.

National Insurance Commission:

Represented on the NHIA Board. Oversees private commercial health insurance.

SSNIT (Social Security and National Insurance Trust):

Transfers 2.5% of member contributions to the NHIS Fund.

Represented on the NHIA Board.

GRA (Ghana Revenue Authority):

Responsible for collecting the 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy.
